coverage_questions: The atlas identifies BIOREASON as one model, while the paper documents four encoder/backbone combinations: Evo2-1B or NT-500M paired with Qwen3-1.7B or Qwen3-4B. Should these combinations be represented as separate trajectories?
The paper does not specify the exact order or chat-template layout used when stacking DNA embeddings, special DNA tokens, and query embeddings.
The paper does not identify the exact DNA tokenizer, special-token IDs, truncation side, or attention masks for each DNA foundation-model variant.
For LLM-only Qwen3 baselines, the paper states that DNA sequences are treated as plain text strings but does not document the tokenizer/template serialization or exact placement of paired sequences.

operation_proposals.why_no_existing_operation: The paper states that Qwen3 baselines receive text queries and DNA sequences as plain text strings, but it does not establish whether the assembly is serialization, concatenation, tokenization, or a specific chat-template sequence.

evidence.quote: BIOREASON operates on two primary input streams: (i) one or more genomic sequences, denoted S DNA; and (ii) textual queries, Q TEXT.
These components are then stacked along the sequence dimension to form the multimodal input X LLM for f LLM.

The proposed BIOREASON models, were evaluated in several f DNA and f LLM combinations. Specifically, we tested Evo2-1B and NT-500M as f DNA encoders, each paired with Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B as f LLM backbones.
